Then one worktree, one task at a time, one commit per task, docs kept truthful. On divergence from the HLD, sync the epic docs before starting the next task. After every task, integrate the branch with `develop` — rebase, then re-verify by tier — before the next one starts. **Review Choice loop.** After the last task, `dev-implementation` runs Gate 4 first. On every PASS it asks the developer whether to **Finish** (Gate 5, then Stage 4) or run a **Cross-model review**: an independent model reviews the epic first, through the Claude CLI or the Codex CLI, which the developer picks every time. The question lists which are on `PATH` and says the repository's content goes to that provider. Option 2 runs `run_external_review.py run` and records each round in `.devtool/epic//review_results.md`, committed after every round. Findings the developer does not accept are `dismissed` only on the developer's explicit words. The mechanics are in `dev-implementation`'s Review Choice section. The invariant is **Gate 4 PASS → Review Choice; Finish → Gate 5; Cross-model review → Gate 4 in full**. After a review round is recorded and all blocking findings have decisions and required Fix commits, Phase 4 starts again with `run_external_review.py check`. Its new PASS presents Review Choice again. The loop ends only when the developer explicitly selects Finish. > [!CRITICAL] > **Mandatory Review Choice loop**: Once every task is `done`, run Gate 4. Cross-model review always returns to a full Gate 4 run before Review Choice is presented again. **Gate 4 Machine Acceptance Criteria:** Gate 4 grants `🟢 LGTM` only when `audit_epic.py` exits 0 — every done task's committed evidence matches its Verification table, and every change to a grader is disclosed — **and** result-based traceability, `check_bdd_traceability.py tests --results` over the HLD's Integration results reports, exits 0 — every scenario in `bdd_scenarios.en.md` proved by an integration test that passed, no test referencing a removed scenario — **and** the provider-based quality orchestrator (`@quality_check`) returns an aggregated verdict of **PASS**, both bound to the exact candidate commit SHA (`git rev-parse HEAD`), with `@quality_check` evaluating all registered providers declared in `.agents/quality/check_quality.json` with profile `epic` against ``. Direct defaults or unprofiled executions are rejected. 2. **Deterministic Aggregation**: All registered providers supporting `epic` must execute or resolve cleanly. Precedence is strict: `FAIL > BLOCKED > PASS`. If any provider returns `FAIL` or `BLOCKED`, the overall verdict is `FAIL` or `BLOCKED`. 3. **No Partial or In-Progress Approvals**: `BLOCKED` cannot transition Gate 4 to approved. Parallel provider executions remain one lifecycle gate; the lifecycle waits for complete aggregate synthesis and never approves on the first provider to finish. 4. **Candidate Immutability**: A 🟢 verdict belongs strictly to the SHA on which the traceability check and quality check ran. A 🟢 verdict belongs to the SHA it ran on. After Gate 4 passes, Review Choice either advances to Gate 5 on **Finish**, or runs a cross-model review and returns to Gate 4 in full. If `develop` moves after the final Gate 4 PASS, Stage 4 rebases the branch and re-verifies it by tier before landing. **Gate 5 Developer Kanban Review & Sign-Off:** Once Gate 4 passes and the developer selects **Finish** at Review Choice, all completed tasks MUST remain in `.devtool/features/done/`. The agent MUST STOP calling tools and present the final executive report to the user. The user visually reviews the Kanban board and approves proceeding to Stage 4. If the user requests adjustments or fixes, the changes land as Fix commits, Gate 4 is re-run in full, and its PASS presents Review Choice again before Gate 5 can recur. ### Stage 4 — Finish Branch → `finishing-a-development-branch` **Entry:** Gate 5 passed (user confirmed). **Exit:** epic branch rebased onto `develop`, re-verified by tier, landed with a `--no-ff` merge, and done tasks archived into `.devtool/epic//`. ## When a Gate Fails | Gate | On failure, return to | |------|----------------------| | 1 | Stage 1 — revise the spec, re-run its self-review | | 2 | Stage 2 — adjust the breakdown; only revisit Stage 1 if scope itself was wrong | | 3 | Stage 3 Phase 1 — reorder by hand; prose notes in task files outrank the calculator | | 4 | Stage 3 — fix findings in the worktree as `[EPIC_NAME] Fix ` commits (done tasks are not reopened), then re-run the traceability check and `quality_check` in full | | 5 | Stage 3 — implement user-requested changes as `[EPIC_NAME] Fix ` commits (done tasks are not reopened), then re-run Gate 4 in full and present Review Choice again before Gate 5 can recur | Never advance on a partial pass, and never re-run only the previously failing check at Gate 4 — the 🟢 verdict must come from a complete run. ## Red Flags - Writing to `implementation_plan.md` or any Antigravity native planning artifact. - Skipping `dev-brainstorming` because "the scope is already clear". - Routing an approved spec straight to an implementation skill, skipping Stage 2 for epic-scale work. - Merging several sub-project specs into one epic directory. - Creating a worktree or dispatching a subagent before Gate 3. new requirements go to dev-designer's Updating an Existing Epic. - Merging to `develop` without a 🟢 from Gate 4. - Granting Gate 4 without a passing traceability check on the same SHA, or without a passing `audit_epic.py`. - Ticking checkboxes or writing evidence by hand instead of running `run_task_checks.py`. - Changing a Verification table, Allowed files or a protected path without stopping to ask. - Skipping the Review Choice after Gate 4 passes, or proceeding directly to Gate 5 without asking the developer to choose Finish or Cross-model review. - Auto-selecting or defaulting the Review Choice on the developer's behalf. - Reusing a Gate 4 PASS after a cross-model review round, finding decision, or Fix commit changed the candidate SHA. - Running the cross-model review without asking the Review Choice. - Starting a cross-model review by picking the review CLI for the developer, instead of asking which of the Claude CLI and the Codex CLI to use. - Writing a `dismissed` decision in `review_results.md` without the developer's words. - Merging to `develop` by hand instead of through `integrate_branch.py land`. - Starting a task while the previous task's integration with `develop` is red. - Invoking `finishing-a-development-branch` without passing Gate 5 (explicit user sign-off after Kanban review). - Archiving tasks from `.devtool/features/done/` prematurely before Gate 5 user review. - Leaving a spec split across `docs/superpowers/specs/` and `.devtool/epic//`. - Producing a durable design document without both language variants or without a complete table of contents. - Using legacy Mermaid syntax (e.g. `graph TD`, `graph LR` instead of `flowchart TD`, `flowchart LR`), unquoted special characters/parentheses in node labels, or malformed Graphviz (DOT) diagrams. - Translating `task_*.md`; task files remain English-only. - Leaving completed `task_*.md` files in `.devtool/features/done/` or draft specs in `docs/superpowers/` after branch integration. ## Rationalizations — STOP and Re-read This Skill | Excuse | Reality | |--------|---------| | "I already have enough context to skip brainstorming" | Context ≠ spec. Gate 1 requires a written, approved spec. | | "This is too simple for the full lifecycle" | Simple work uses `dev-brainstorming` → `writing-plans`. You still start at Stage 1. | | "I'll just write the implementation plan directly" | `implementation_plan.md` is an Antigravity artifact. d3nexus uses `docs/superpowers/specs/` and `.devtool/`. | | "The user confirmed the scope, that's basically Gate 1" | Gate 1 is spec approval through `dev-brainstorming`, not a scope question. | | "I can combine research + spec into one step" | Stage 1 is `dev-brainstorming`'s job. Invoke the skill. | | "The developer obviously wants to continue" | The Handoff Choice is theirs. Ask it every time a new epic passes Gate 2. | | "Gate 4 passed once, so I can finish after the review" | A review round or its decisions change the candidate SHA. Run Gate 4 in full and present Review Choice again. | | "The developer probably just wants to finish" | The developer chooses every time. Never assume Finish or pick on their behalf. | ## Stage Skills | Stage | Skill | Gate it enforces | |-------|-------|------------------| | 1 | `dev-brainstorming` | 1 | | 2 | `dev-designer` | 2 | | 3 | `dev-implementation` | 3, triggers 4, and enforces 5 | | 3 (verification) | `quality_check` + `check_bdd_traceability.py` | 4 | | 4 | `finishing-a-development-branch` | — | ' : skills/dev-lifecycle/SKILL.md must not contain Mermaid diagram fences
